functions.function: archive package integrity and retrieval verification
intended_uses: create an immutable SHA-256-indexed package from the exact required CI artifacts
detect missing, extra, tampered, unsafe-path, case-colliding, stale-control, or wrong-commit package content
compare primary verification with a separately implemented host-native digest verifier
publish and retrieve without overwrite through an unconfigured technical-trial filesystem adapter
prohibited_uses: claim GitHub Actions is a controlled external archive
promote evidence without independent and release controls
inputs: exact required CI artifact directories including target-object inventories
outputs: primary and independent internal retrieval results
functions.affected_process: lifecycle-data staging, integrity verification, and retrieval rehearsal

activity_effect.detail: Automates byte inventory and integrity checks but does not eliminate archive-owner review or controlled-archive procedures.

failure_modes.description: required artifacts are omitted, substituted, or supplemented
artifact bytes or manifest metadata change after packaging
path traversal, symbolic links, or case collisions redirect or obscure evidence
ephemeral storage expires or lacks approved access, backup, retention, or disposition controls
detection_controls: open control items and promotion blocker

failure_modes.description: concurrent publication or a receipt-write failure leaves an ambiguous or partially published package

fallback.procedure: Retain the failed verification result, prohibit promotion, retrieve a second copy when available, compare against the exact source run, and regenerate only from the clean source workflow after discrepancy resolution.

functions.residual_reliance: Repository permissions, GitHub retention, archive ownership, backup, disposition, and external retrieval acceptance remain outside the tool's verified boundary.
limitations: Internal staging and technical-trial transport only
No designated controlled external archive
No approved retention or disposition authority
Separate verifier reduces common mode but does not supply qualified or organizationally independent verification

functions.function: Windows native-fault activation and evidence collection
intended_uses: retain native exits, scenario oracles, host identity, and artifact hashes
prohibited_uses: target unrelated operating-system or filesystem drivers
treat optional Application Verifier output as mandatory baseline evidence
inputs: optional elevated disposable Application Verifier host

activity_effect.detail: Automates repeatable scenario execution but preserves independent expected-result and applicability review.

failure_modes.description: the intended Windows error is not activated or a different error is accepted
wrong host, source revision, target, toolchain, or command is used
detection_controls: exact commit, tree, host, target, toolchain, and command validation

failure_modes.description: Application Verifier cannot be elevated, activated, queried, cleaned, or timed out safely
a prior independent review is reused after affected candidate inputs change
detection_controls: candidate commit and manifest digest binding

fallback.procedure: Retain failed or indeterminate output, use the deterministic Win32-boundary matrix as minimum technical evidence, repeat on a clean Windows host, and prohibit closure until the exact candidate receives its own independent review.

functions.residual_reliance: Independent expected-result review, host applicability, external archive acceptance, and broader organizational independence remain required outside the collector.
limitations: No kernel-mode Driver Verifier applicability
Application Verifier requires an elevated disposable host
Review approval is candidate-specific
Internal evidence only
